attempts.paper_title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Modulates Feedforward and Feedback Cortico-Thalamo-Cortical Pathways by Selectively Activating Excitatory Neurons
attempts.entry_title: Transcranial focused ultrasound and S1 spiking (Gao et al. 2025) on dandiset 000637
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data. Its claims on PRF and duty-cycle dependent responses of regular-spiking and fast-spiking units in S1 and POm, and on S1 to POm correlations, all need the cell-type split, but the Units tables hold spike times only, with no waveforms. Most also need POm or auditory cortex units, sham or CG1 sessions, or duty cycles the dandiset lacks. The recordings could not be linked to the paper's, which names another dandiset, and S1 units here number 4,642 against the paper's 1,297. Pooled across cell types, every PRF raised S1 firing during sonication, which decides nothing.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Ramachandran, Yu and He (2025) on dandiset 000637, which holds spike times of sorted S1 units from 25 rats under tFUS at five PRFs and several pulse durations. Every claim is about units typed as RSU or FSU from their waveforms, which the dandiset lacks, and most also need POm or auditory cortex units, so all claims are blocked. The notebook checks the metadata against the data, the trial clock and the unit counts, and shows the responses of all S1 units pooled.

outcomes.notes: The dandiset's Units tables hold spike times only, with no waveforms, waveform features, electrodes or cell-type labels (data check), so units cannot be classified as RSUs or FSUs by the initial phase and afterhyperpolarization of their waveforms (Methods, Neuronal type classification). The waveforms of these units are not public anywhere else that the attempt could find; the paper's data statement names dandiset 000946, whose rats (BH494 to BH594, 20 rats) are not those of 000637 (BH401 to BH477). No recording holds POm units (each file has one 32-channel probe with electrode locations 'unknown', and the description names only S1). As a variant, S1 units with more than 2,000 spikes, all cell types together, number 4,642 in the PRF series at 200 us (4,023 at 5 V), 1,088 at 3000 Hz and 862 at 30 Hz, against the paper's S1 RSU plus FSU sums of 1,297, 366 and 209, about 3.6 times as many; so the dataset's units are not, or not only, the units the paper counted. The S1 totals already rule out reproduced whatever classification were applied. Each S1 RSU plus FSU pair would sum to the dataset's total (4,642, 1,088, 862) against the paper's 1,297, 366 and 209, so at most one count of each S1 pair could match, at most 9 of the 12 counts in all, below the criterion's 10. The outcome stays blocked because the six POm counts cannot be computed. The paper's two groups total 28 rats (16 and 12, Methods), the dataset 25.

findings.statement: The Units tables hold spike times only, with no waveforms, waveform features, electrode assignments or quality metrics, so the units cannot be classified as regular- or fast-spiking as the paper does, and every finding of the paper is about one or the other.

The dandiset holds one S1 probe per recording. It has no POm or auditory cortex units, no recording identified as sham or as targeting CG1, and of the paper's duty-cycle series only the four conditions whose pulse duration is 100, 200 or 400 us, the three pulse durations the description lists (3000 Hz at 30 and 60%, 30 Hz at 0.6%, 1500 Hz at 60%).

The recordings cannot be linked to those the paper analysed. The paper's data statement names dandiset 000946, whose rats (BH494 to BH594, 20 rats) are not those of 000637 (BH401 to BH477), and 000637 has about 3.6 times as many S1 units over the paper's 2,000 spike threshold in the PRF series at 200 us as the paper reports S1 RSUs and FSUs (4,642 against 1,297). Which of these recordings, if any, the paper used is not stated.
The description says each recording has 500 trials; 73 of the 292 files have fewer (230 in 45 files, 425 in 13, 375 in 11, and 252 to 400 in four).

The description calls 100, 200 and 400 us the ultrasound durations (UDs) and says the pulse duration was kept at 67 ms; in the paper's terms and in the file identifiers these are the pulse durations and 67 ms is the ultrasound duration. A 600 us recording (BH446) and recordings at 3.5, 5.5 and 7 V are present and not described.

The stimulation condition is coded only in each file's identifier (PRF, pulse duration, ultrasound duration, voltage, repeat); the trials tables have start and stop times only, the electrode locations are all 'unknown' (the one electrode group's location is 'brain area', every electrode has z = 0, and no file has experiment_description, notes, stimulus or protocol fields), and three recordings named BASELINE are not described (whether tFUS was off, how their trial times were made).
